mixed_attack_and_fault.pcap.description: An attacker intercepts a laptop (and slows it down) while the NAS is down.

clean.pcap.description: A normal two-minute office capture with no problems.

arp_spoof.pcap.description: A device pretends to be the router to intercept a laptop's traffic.

duplicate_ip.pcap.description: Two devices were given the same IP address by mistake.

port_scan.pcap.description: A device scans another for open ports (Nmap-style SYN scan).

rogue_dhcp_dns_hijack.pcap.description: A fake DHCP server makes itself the DNS server and redirects github.com.

dns_failures.pcap.description: The router's DNS stops answering for a while, then returns errors.

tcp_retransmissions.pcap.description: A laptop on weak Wi-Fi keeps losing packets.

malicious_xss_dnsname.pcap.description: Malicious input: DNS names containing <script> code (must display as text).

slow_handshakes.pcap.description: A busy web server takes seconds to accept connections.

tcp_resets_service_down.pcap.description: The file-sharing service on the office NAS has stopped.

broken_truncated.pcap.description: Damaged input: a capture cut off in the middle of a packet.

not_a_pcap.pcap.description: Wrong input: a web page renamed to .pcap (must be rejected).
